description: Would this workflow graph run? Returns the blocking errors — an unknown tool, a wire into a port that does not exist, a cycle — each naming the node and the port, without running anything.

_files.description: The project's files, standing in for the project open in the editor: each is one record reference (a `file`, `sample`, `accession` or named `sequence`). Every sequence record they hold becomes a library document a tool can name in its `sequences`/`parts`/`document` arguments (a multi-record file as `file · record`), and a tool reading a file by name (a trace, an alignment) finds it here.

accession.description: an archive accession, fetched and parsed with its annotations, e.g. NC_005816, U49845, P38398, BBa_R0040. `search_records` finds one.

features.description: with `sequence`: INSDC-style features {name, type, start, end, strand}, if you have them

file.description: a file you hold: {name, text} for a text format (GenBank, FASTA, EMBL, GFF, Clustal…) or {name, base64} for any file, binary ones (.dna, .ab1, .xdna) included. The extension of `name` is how the format is read.

name.description: with `sequence`: a label for the record

record_index.description: which record of a multi-record source (0-based). A `_subject` holding several records and no index is refused with the list to choose from.

sample.description: a bundled sample, by the id `list_samples` returns (or its file name when unique)

_subject.description: The record this call acts on, standing in for the document open in the editor. Exactly one of: `sequence`, `file`, `sample`, `accession`. This server holds no project, so a tool needing a subject gets it here or refuses by name.

graph.description: A workflow graph: nodes naming tools, wires carrying one node’s output into another’s input, and the two constructs a single tool call cannot express — `$whenExpression` (run this node only if…) and `scatter` (run it once per element of a list input, gathering every output into an array).

edges.description: the wires: `{ id, from: { node, port }, to: { node, port } }`, naming a node by its `id` and a port by the output or input name the tool listing gives. Wire an output into `$subject` to hand the product downstream, or into `$when` to gate a step on an upstream result.

name.description: a label for the run record

nodes.description: one entry per step: `{ id, tool, params }`, where `params` are that tool’s own arguments as the tool listing documents them. Add `"$whenExpression": "subject.length > 500"` to make the step conditional — Operators: == != < > <= >= and or not && || ! + - * / % ?? (`and`/`or`/`not` are the words for `&&`/`||`/`!`). Functions: abs, ceil, contains, floor, isset, len, lower, max, min, number, round, upper. Property access and indexing work (`subject.length`, `rows[0].name`); method calls do not, and there is no ternary — a condition returns one verdict. — or `scatter: ["port"]` to run it once per element of that input.

name: validate_workflow
